query: Consider the following context: High-temperature self-lubricating materials with stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range are essential for advanced mechanical systems under extreme conditions. However, balancing mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency remains a key challenge. In that context, which material can be used for high-performance wide-temperature self-lubricating materials, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A high-temperature self-lubricating material composed of a titanium carbide (TiC) matrix with added solid lubricant phases of calcium fluoride (CaF2) and graphite will exhibit stable tribological performance across a wide temperature range.
generation.material_initial_state: TiC matrix with 10 vol% CaF2 and 5 vol% graphite, sintered at 1200°C for 2 hours
generation.intervention: Adding 10 vol% CaF2 and 5 vol% graphite to the TiC matrix
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 200-800°C, sliding speed: 0.5 m/s, normal load: 10 N
generation.structural_mediator: The solid lubricant phases of CaF2 and graphite will form a tribofilm on the wear surface, reducing friction and wear
generation.mechanism: The CaF2 and graphite phases will deform and flow at high temperatures, providing a continuous lubricating film and reducing the coefficient of friction
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in coefficient of friction by 30% and a decrease in wear rate by 50% compared to the baseline TiC material without solid lubricant phases
generation.baseline: TiC material without solid lubricant phases, tested under the same conditions
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 200-800°C, sliding speed: 0.5 m/s, normal load: 10 N
generation.uncertainty: The actual performance of the material may vary depending on the specific processing conditions and the properties of the starting materials. The stability of the tribofilm and the lubricating properties of the CaF2 and graphite phases at high temperatures may also affect the outcome.

falsification_experiment.design: Sliding wear test using a ball-on-disk tribometer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coefficient of friction is not reduced by at least 20% and the wear rate is not decreased by at least 30% compared to the baseline material, the hypothesis is falsified.
